text:
maria_support: Heads-up — we're getting multiple customer tickets about higher p95/p99 on text-generation endpoints since the 02:00 UTC deploy. Customers report sudden 2-3x latency regressions for long context requests. Example request_id=rid_0a9f3, customer=acme-inc, model=redwood-v1-4b@quantized:balanced:int8

alex_runtime: Thanks Maria. Do we have any perf dashboards or traces? Which clusters are affected? Any correlation with model variants or quant profiles?

maria_support: Linking the customer trace we attached: https://redwood.internal/traces/rid_0a9f3 (private). Affected: hosted-us-west-2 and a Dedicated pool in eu-west-1. The customer is using the quantized variant `redwood-v1-4b:balanced-int8` — they say they didn't change prompts.

srebot: Alert: latency_p99 spike on route `/v1/generate` (hosted-us-west-2) at 2025-11-20T02:15Z — p99 jumped from 320ms -> 980ms. Related deploy: deploy-20251120-quant-profiles-v2.

alex_runtime: Good catch from the bot. I saw the deploy tag — we enabled a new quantization profile rollout (`balanced:int8` default for some model families) as part of that. Quick hypothesis: int8 path causing more kernel thrashing for long sequences or KV cache layout changed. Need traces and kernel-level metrics. Jin, did ML ops run any post-quant perf validation?

jin_ml: I ran offline perf sims but on synthetic short-context workloads. We did run a calibration job for int8 profiles; however, we also enabled an fp8-experimental toggle for a small canary yesterday. The canary target was 10% but looks like routing rules pushed more requests to the quantized variant in some regions. Calibration logs show occasional large variance in activations for some attention heads — likely causing dynamic dequant/fallbacks.

maria_support: Customer supplied a repro curl. Repro steps I ran: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-4b:balanced-int8","input":"<~2k tokens prompt>"}'
```
Result: p95~1.0s from hosted-us-west-2. When I forced model `redwood-v1-4b:fp16` it dropped to p95~330ms.

alex_runtime: That matches the hypothesis. We need an immediate mitigation: pin affected routes/customers to fp16 and rollback canary rollout for the quant profile. Sam, can we hotfix routing or apply a per-customer model override?

sam_ops: Yep. We can set a per-customer override in the routing config and push a hot route that maps acme-inc and other impacted customers to `redwood-v1-4b:fp16`. I can do that now. Also propose throttling the quantized variant by setting `max_concurrency=1` as a temporary limiter.

jin_ml: While ops mitigates, we should also disable fp8-experimental and re-run calibration on representative long-context traces. My takeaway: calibration on short sequences didn't reveal the tail behavior. We'll add a distribution-weighted calibration using production traces (sanitized) and re-measure head-wise scale/clipping.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollback-quant-canary -> target: hosted-us-west-2, eu-west-1 (initiated by sam_ops). CI checks: quick smoke + canary-health.

alex_runtime: Action list:
- sam_ops: apply per-customer override to fp16 and throttle quantized variant (ETA 15m).
- jin_ml: disable fp8 toggle and start extended calibration using sampled long-context traces (ETA 2 days).
- alex_runtime + infra: gather kernel metrics (cupti/metrics) and KV cache stats, look for extra memcpy or kernel re-launch counts (ETA 1h).
- maria_support: compile impacted customer list and repro logs (ETA 30m).

maria_support: Adding customer list now, sending to the thread. Will also reply to acme ticket with mitigation steps and eta.

alex_runtime: For reproducibility — here's the runtime flag you can use to force FP16 on a specific serving process if you need an immediate local repro: 
```
# start a local runtime process pinned to fp16
./redwood-runtime --model redwood-v1-4b --quantization disabled --force-fp16 true --log-level debug
```

jin_ml: For calibration repro: use these steps to generate an activation distribution dump from prod traces (sanitized):
```
# sample traces (internal tool)
redwood-trace-sampler --route /v1/generate --since 2025-11-19T00:00Z --max 5000 > samples.json
# run calibration script
python tools/calibrate_quant.py --model redwood-v1-4b --samples samples.json --out cal_profile_v2.json
```

Note: the current `cal_profile_v1.json` was generated from mostly <=512 token workloads. We'll add tail-weighting.

sam_ops: Rollback applied and overrides pushed. Throttled quant-variant to 1 concurrent request in hosted-us-west-2 as an extra precaution. Monitoring now — initial p99 dropping back toward baseline.

srebot: Alert resolved: latency_p99 back to normal range on `/v1/generate` (hosted-us-west-2).

cara_product: Thanks team. Can we capture this in an incident write-up and include a note for product: avoid enabling default quant profile rollouts without long-tail calibration? I'll coordinate the customer comms template.

alex_runtime: Agreed — I'll own the technical postmortem. Quick notes to include: mis-scoped calibration, unexpected routing weight in canary, kernel-level dynamic fallbacks on int8->fp16 dequant paths. Proposed long-term: per-workload calibration, improved canary throttles, and a runtime metric exposing 'dequant_fallback_count' so we can alert earlier.

maria_support: I'll update acme's ticket and attach the workaround. Thanks everyone.

jin_ml: I'll start the extended calibration runs and also add an automated regression test that uses long-context sequences. Will paste results when ready.

alex_runtime: Nice work. Closing loop: once jin_ml posts calibration findings, we'll plan controlled re-rollout with staged concurrency limits and additional observability (dequant counters).
